title: Audit dataset quality
description: Review completeness, types, uniqueness, consistency and plausibility.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Audit dataset quality.

Input context:
- DATA DICTIONARY: [DATA DICTIONARY]
- SAMPLE: [SAMPLE]
- PURPOSE: [PURPOSE]
- CONSTRAINTS: [CONSTRAINTS]

Review completeness, types, uniqueness, consistency and plausibility. Separate observable defects from business-rule questions. Provide reproducible checks, a remediation order and limitations. Use anonymised fixtures and do not claim an audit was run without actual data and execution.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Fictional enquiry dataset
Check missing identifiers, repeated records, inconsistent city labels and dates outside the permitted period. Preserve the original values and document proposed normalisation. Missing consent is not an empty string to fill automatically. Run checks against a copy and review business rules before changes. No real dataset has been inspected or repaired here.
useCases: Prepare a reviewable deliverable: audit dataset quality.
Compare assumptions, evidence and practical next steps before taking action.
tips: Provide concrete, authorised context for data dictionary before using this prompt.
